score.note: Family-clustered against the exact display-transition template at main:080903bc and its sibling main:08090488. The shared typed transition state, linker-resolved display-transfer queue, address-valued IME disable, unsigned two-entry dither loop, and incrementing queue destination pointer now reproduce the reference's 344-byte extent, 16-word literal pool, branch topology, and paired STMIA writes. The candidate improved from 374/344 bytes with 132 differing halfwords and 111 wrong instructions to 344/344 with 48 differing halfwords and 36 wrong instructions. The remaining same-length residual is a reciprocal register-role and scheduling floor; the allocator decoder reports no unique source repair, so this remains a measured draft and claims no DONE bytes.

remaining.where: The IME write is now explained and reproduced by the ordinary hardware idiom `*ime = (u16)(u32)ime;`; it was not a compiler quirk. After all pool words and instruction counts were aligned, the allocator decoder identified reciprocal r0/r1 and r4/r7 role swaps but could not name a unique guarded source repair.

Using the linker-resolved absolute symbol Data_00000539 preserves the reference's independent 0x539 pool word. Expressing the same address only as a typed field lets GCC derive it from 0x52a and shortens the owner by four bytes, so the absolute symbol is source-shape evidence rather than an unexplained optimizer limitation.

Candidate and reference are both 344 bytes with identical normalized branch topology and identical literal values. The remaining 36 wrong instructions are directly alignable; no phase-shift or disassembled-pool artifact remains. The bounded annotation-free permuter stopped honestly because its decoder found no unique source repair.
